before.description_long:
Gemini is Google's family of AI models and the consumer assistant built on top of them, available on the web, in the mobile app, and woven into Workspace apps like Gmail, Docs and Sheets. It handles conversation, long-document analysis, image and video generation, coding, and live voice interaction.

As of mid-2026 the default model is Gemini 3.8 Flash, which reached general availability on May 19, 2026 with strong agentic and coding performance. The heavier reasoning and coding work is handled by Gemini 3.1 Pro, now the flagship model. Google also shipped Gemini Omni for native video generation and editing (May 2026) and Gemini Spark, an autonomous agent (June 2026). Note that the Gemini 3.5 Pro general release slipped to July 2026.

Capabilities span text and code generation, native image and video creation, Deep Research for multi-source reports, and Gemini Live for real-time spoken conversation. The models are natively multimodal and can work over very long contexts, which suits large codebases and long documents.

Pricing is freemium. The free tier costs nothing and includes Gemini 3.8 Flash, limited daily access to Gemini 3.1 Pro, image and video generation, Deep Research and Gemini Live. Google AI Plus is $7.99/mo, Google AI Pro is $19.99/mo (the former Gemini Advanced / Google AI Premium, with 2TB storage and higher limits), and Google AI Ultra now comes in two tiers: a $100/mo entry tier launched May 19, 2026 and a $200/mo top tier (cut from $250 at I/O 2026). The Gemini API is billed per token, roughly $2 per million input tokens and $12 per million output tokens for Gemini 3-class models.

Limitations are worth noting: free-tier access to the strongest model is capped daily, the naming across models and subscription tiers is genuinely confusing, and the top-end features sit behind expensive Ultra plans. Availability of some newer features can also vary by region.

Gemini is a good fit for people already inside Google's ecosystem, for anyone who wants image and video generation plus chat in one place, and for developers who want to build on a pay-per-token multimodal API.

ChatGPT is OpenAI's flagship chat assistant for writing, coding, research, analysis and multimodal tasks. It works in the browser, in desktop and mobile apps, and through the API, and remains one of the most widely used consumer AI products.

As of October 2026, OpenAI's model picker lists GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna alongside the older GPT-5.6 Sol, Sol Pro, Terra and Luna, plus GPT-5 Thinking Mini. GPT-6 Astra is the current flagship, released September 3, 2026; GPT-6 Sol and Luna followed on September 22, 2026. Per OpenAI, quoted by MacRumors, GPT-6 Sol and Luna are not yet available in standard Chat mode and currently launch first in ChatGPT Work and Codex. On Free and Go, GPT-6 Luna is available only in the desktop app. The exact default chat model was not independently verified.

Capabilities span long-form and technical writing, code generation and debugging, document and image analysis, voice conversations, web browsing, data analysis, and image generation.

Pricing is tiered. Free is $0/mo, with unlimited text chats on GPT-6 Luna (desktop app only) subject to abuse limits, plus limited uploads, image creation, voice, deep research and Codex use; the free plan is ad-supported for logged-in adults in the US. A paid Go tier also exists and may include advertising, and a paid Plus tier adds advanced reasoning with GPT-6, projects, scheduled tasks, custom GPTs and more Codex usage; neither tier's USD price could be confirmed, since OpenAI's pricing page was geo-served in ILS at the time of checking. Above that, Pro is offered in three monthly-only tiers: $100, $200 and $500 per month, with only the $500 tier including GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast. Business and Enterprise plans exist but current verified USD pricing for them was not available.

Limitations remain real: the model can still produce confident but incorrect answers, the free and Go tiers carry ads, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna are still rolling out, with full Chat-mode availability not yet confirmed. Go and Plus pricing is also not transparently published in USD everywhere, which can make budgeting harder for US buyers.

ChatGPT suits anyone who wants a general-purpose AI assistant, from casual users on the ad-supported free plan to professionals and teams who need the paid tiers for larger quotas, advanced reasoning or higher-usage Pro plans.

Claude is a conversational AI assistant from Anthropic, used through the web app, mobile apps, and the API. It handles long-form writing, analysis, coding, document reading, and multi-step reasoning, with an emphasis on careful, steerable responses.

The current model lineup is Claude Fable 5.1 (flagship), Claude Opus 5.5 for complex agentic coding and enterprise work, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and the lighter Claude Haiku 4.5. A separate Claude Mythos 5.1 exists but has limited availability through the invitation-only Project Glasswing program.

Context window size varies by model: Claude 4.6-generation models and later support up to a 1M-token context window, which helps with large codebases, long documents, or full transcripts in one conversation. Haiku 4.5 predates that generation and does not carry the same context size. The models also support multimodal input and tool use across the product.

Pricing is tiered. The Free plan is $0, with usage caps, and includes web/desktop/mobile chat, web search, file creation, code execution, memory, connectors, and artifacts. Pro is $20/month billed monthly, or $17/month if billed annually ($200 charged up front). Max starts from $100/month for expanded usage; higher usage tiers are referenced on Anthropic's pricing page but a specific price above $100/month is not published. Team offers a Standard seat at $25/month billed monthly ($20/month billed annually) and a Premium seat at $125/month billed monthly ($100/month billed annually), with a two-seat minimum. Enterprise is listed at $20/seat/month plus usage billed at API rates, billed annually. API list pricing per million tokens is $10/$50 for Fable 5.1, $4/$20 for Opus 5.5, $2/$10 for Sonnet 5.5, $1/$5 for Haiku 4.5, and $10/$50 for Mythos 5.1 (invitation only).

Limitations are worth noting. Free and paid plans carry usage caps that reset on a rolling basis, so heavy users can hit limits mid-session. Haiku 4.5 does not offer the larger context window available on newer models, and the top-end Mythos 5.1 is not openly available. As with any LLM, outputs still need checking for factual accuracy.

Claude suits writers, developers, analysts, and teams who want strong reasoning, large-context handling on supported models, and a choice of models to balance cost against capability.

before.description: Meta AI is Meta's assistant built into WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, Threads and its AI glasses, and remains free for everyday use. As of April 2026 it runs on Muse Spark, Meta Superintelligence Labs' first proprietary model, replacing the earlier Llama-based engine.
before.description_long:
Meta AI is the conversational assistant that Meta ships across its apps rather than as a standalone product. You reach it inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger and Threads, and through Meta's AI glasses, so it sits wherever people already chat and browse.

The underlying model changed in 2026. Since an April 8, 2026 announcement, Meta AI runs on Muse Spark, the first proprietary large language model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, replacing the earlier Llama-based engine. In September 2026 Meta also launched Muse, a separate personal AI agent app also powered by Muse Spark, available at muse.ai and through WhatsApp with a US rollout.

Day to day, the assistant answers questions, drafts and rewrites text, summarizes threads, and helps in group chats, acting on the context you are already looking at instead of forcing you into a separate window.

Meta states that the core Meta AI experience remains free for everyday use. On September 15, 2026, Meta launched Meta One worldwide, a subscription system that adds more usage of compute-heavy AI features. It includes single-app "Plus" plans for WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook, multi-app consumer bundles called Meta One Core and Meta One Premium, and business/creator tiers called Essential, Advanced, Expert and Max. Meta's own published prices are in euros; US-dollar figures circulating for these tiers come from third-party reports and are not confirmed on Meta's primary pricing pages.

The main limitations are the ones that come with a closed, platform-bound assistant: the shift to the proprietary Muse Spark ended the open-weight approach many developers relied on, the tier structure and naming are more complex now that single-app and multi-app plans coexist, and Meta AI is tied to Meta's ecosystem rather than being a standalone tool you can host yourself.

It is a natural fit if you already live in WhatsApp, Instagram or Messenger and want an assistant right there, and are fine with a proprietary model and Meta's data practices. If you specifically want open weights or a standalone workspace, look elsewhere.

before.description_long:
Notion AI is the artificial-intelligence layer inside Notion, the document and database workspace. It lives directly in your pages, so instead of switching to a separate chatbot you summon it where your notes, wikis and project databases already are.

The current release is Notion 3.7, shipped September 15, 2026. It adds an agent Skills system with a skills library, the ability to export Skills to external tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Grok, Custom Agents that can call sub-agents, a Notion Agents iOS app, and a redesigned model picker that lets workspace owners choose which models are available to the built-in Notion Agent versus Custom Agents, drawing on several AI vendors. The prior 3.6 release (July 2026) introduced orchestration of External Agents such as Claude and Cursor from shared boards, AI-generated interactive HTML blocks, reading and writing Microsoft Office files (PPTX, XLSX, DOCX) and Outlook, AI Meeting Notes with speaker identification, Enterprise Search across connected apps, and a Research Mode.

Day to day the AI can draft and rewrite text, translate, summarize long pages, fill and query databases, answer questions across your whole workspace, and run multi-step agent tasks. Custom Agents you build yourself are billed on a credit system, free to try and then $10 per 1,000 monthly Notion credits, and their activity can be tracked through audit logging on higher plans.

Pricing has four tiers. Free is $0 per member per month but only includes a capped trial of Notion AI, not ongoing access. Plus is $10 per seat per month billed annually (about $12 per seat per month if billed monthly) and also only includes the AI trial. Business is $20 per seat per month billed annually (about $24 per seat per month if billed monthly) and is the cheapest plan with full, ongoing AI, including the Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search. Enterprise is custom-priced and adds zero data retention with LLM providers. Notion AI is not sold as a separate add-on; it is bundled into the Business and Enterprise seat price, with Custom Agent credits as an extra variable cost.

The main catch is that ongoing AI access sits behind the Business plan. Free and Plus users only get a capped AI trial, so casual users who expect free or cheap AI on their existing workspace will hit a wall quickly. Custom Agent credits are an added, usage-based cost on top of seat pricing, and some higher-end features such as audit logging are reserved for upper tiers.

Notion AI makes most sense for teams already running their knowledge base, docs and projects in Notion who want AI in the same place and are on or willing to move to the Business tier. Solo note-takers on the free or Plus plan will find the AI too limited to rely on day to day.

before.description: Microsoft Copilot (formerly the Microsoft 365 Copilot app) is Microsoft's AI assistant integrated across Windows, Edge, Bing, and the Microsoft 365 apps, with a model selector offering Auto, Quick response, and Think deeper modes.
before.description_long:
Microsoft Copilot is the AI assistant Microsoft has woven across Windows, Edge, Bing, and the Microsoft 365 apps. It was recently renamed: the Microsoft 365 Copilot app is now called Microsoft Copilot, and the Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat app is now called Microsoft Copilot Chat. It handles conversational chat, web search, image generation, document drafting, and in licensed tiers it works directly inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Licensing is organized into tiers: Copilot Chat (Basic), Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic), which gives standard Copilot access inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote without a separate add-on, and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), an add-on with expanded access. Microsoft has also introduced Copilot Cowork, a usage-based product for broader agentic work, and Microsoft 365 E7 enterprise plans include Copilot licensing by default.

Day to day, Copilot routes requests through a model selector with Auto, Quick response, and Think deeper options rather than exposing specific model version numbers. Anthropic's Claude models are also available in applicable licensed experiences; Word's model menu, for example, now includes an Anthropic model as the default for higher-reasoning tasks. Copilot Cowork has also gained new image-generation capability from a third-party model provider.

Pricing could not be verified on Microsoft's own pricing pages at the time of this review, so specific dollar figures are omitted here. What is confirmed is the tier structure above: a basic chat experience, a basic in-app tier, a paid Premium add-on, and the newer usage-based Cowork product. Copilot Chat (Basic) is included at no extra cost for users with an eligible Microsoft 365 work subscription, but this is not a standalone free plan open to the general public.

The main limitations are that Microsoft's licensing and naming are genuinely hard to follow across consumer, Business, and enterprise SKUs, current pricing is not transparently published, and the strongest in-app features require a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license rather than being available to casual users. Copilot makes the most sense for people and organizations already inside Microsoft 365 who want an assistant that reaches into their documents, mail, and calendar rather than a standalone chatbot.
